One particular work comes to mind, a grand opera I composed in my youth, filled with lofty aspirations and grand ideas. However, upon reflection and with the passage of time, it became clear that my craftsmanship had not yet reached the level necessary to fully realize the vision I had set forth. The result was a work that fell short of my intentions, a humbling experience for a young composer eager to make his mark.

In the face of this perceived failure, I did not retreat into despondency or self-pity. Instead, I embraced the opportunity for growth and learning. I delved deeper into my studies, honing my skills in composition, orchestration, and musical theory. I sought out mentors and collaborators who could offer guidance and wisdom. Through diligence and perseverance, I endeavored to bridge the gap between my aspirations and my capabilities.

This experience taught me a valuable lesson about the importance of humility and self-awareness in the pursuit of artistic excellence. It reminded me that true mastery is not achieved through pride or arrogance, but through a willingness to acknowledge one's limitations and work tirelessly to overcome them. It instilled in me a sense of discipline and dedication that continues to guide my artistic endeavors to this day.

I am grateful for the opportunity to reflect on this pivotal moment in my artistic journey, and I stand before you today as a composer who has embraced the lessons of failure with humility and gratitude. Thank you for considering my candid response.

Ah, I am grateful for your kind words, esteemed committee members. During my formative years in Vienna, I was fortunate to have the guidance and mentorship of the esteemed composer Christoph Willibald Gluck. His musical wisdom and artistic insight left a lasting impression on me and significantly influenced my development as a composer.

Working closely with Gluck, I learned the importance of clarity and emotional depth in musical expression. He taught me the significance of serving the dramatic narrative through music, emphasizing the power of simplicity and sincerity in composition. These lessons have continued to shape my approach to composition, inspiring me to prioritize the emotional impact and coherence of my works.

Furthermore, Gluck's emphasis on the integration of music and drama encouraged me to explore new ways of blending vocal and instrumental elements to create a seamless and evocative musical tapestry. His mentorship instilled in me a deep appreciation for the dramatic potential of music and the transformative effect it can have on the listener.

The influence of Gluck's teachings continues to resonate in my compositions today, guiding me in my quest to create works that are not only technically proficient but also emotionally resonant and artistically compelling. I am forever grateful for the invaluable lessons I learned from him, lessons that have become an integral part of my musical identity.
